cells.Values and default: Integer number of nanoseconds, parsed with `std::stoi`. Text that does not start with a number makes `std::stoi` throw an exception. Unset: 500 nanoseconds.
cells.Effect: Sets the wait length that the main thread of the spin-wait benchmark (a test loop that polls a flag and does not sleep) gives to the CPU instruction `tpause`. The worker thread always uses 500 nanoseconds. Read only when `PAUSE_TYPE` is `tpause`. A negative number becomes a very large unsigned number. The test passes the length in CPU cycles as the deadline of `intel_tpause`. `h/system/mwaitx.hpp` describes that deadline as a target value of the time-stamp counter (TSC), not a length.

hints.problem: Rule 6, and the rule on vague words. "very large" gives no number. The code stores the value in an unsigned 64-bit type (`size_t` or `uint64_t`), so `-1` becomes 2^64 - 1. Checked in t/t_mwaitx.cpp:729 and :746. Original phrase: "A negative number becomes a very large unsigned number."
hints.suggested: Replace the whole cell with: Sets the wait length that the main thread of the spin-wait benchmark (a test loop that polls a flag and does not sleep) gives to the CPU instruction `tpause`. The worker thread always uses 500 nanoseconds. Read only when `PAUSE_TYPE` is `tpause`. A negative number converts to an unsigned 64-bit number. `-1` becomes about 1.8 x 10^19 nanoseconds. The test passes the length in CPU cycles as the deadline of `intel_tpause`. `h/system/mwaitx.hpp` describes that deadline as a target value of the time-stamp counter (TSC), not a length.

cells.Values and default: `tpause` selects the CPU instruction `tpause`. `none` selects a loop with no pause instruction. Any other text keeps the default. The match is exact. Unset: the CPU instruction `pause`.
cells.Effect: Chooses the wait instruction of the spin-wait benchmark (a test loop that polls a flag and does not sleep). The test case is `spin-wait loop with Intel pause/tpause`. The test case skips on a CPU whose vendor is not Intel. `PAUSE_HINT` and `PAUSE_LEN_NS` are read only with `tpause`. The test requires an average wait of at most 35 nanoseconds with `pause`, 36 nanoseconds with `tpause` and 45 nanoseconds with `none`.

cells.Values and default: Any value turns it on, also an empty one. The text is not parsed. Unset: the flag `verbose_test` is false.

The file does not call that macro. No output changes. `t/CMakeLists.txt` registers `t_hwattention_replay` with `DISABLED TRUE`.

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed by `std::stoul` with base 0: decimal, `0x` prefix for hexadecimal, `0` prefix for octal. Only the low 16 bits count. Text without a leading number throws an exception. Unset: `0`. The test writes zeros over the KV cache region of the HBM (the memory on each FPGA card). Empty: `std::stoul` throws an exception.
cells.Effect: The test writes the low 16 bits of the value as a repeated pattern over the weight region of the HBM. It does this on every FPGA card that it opens. A value whose low 16 bits are 0 gives the unset behaviour. Both modes overwrite memory on every FPGA card that the test opens. libpos reads `SYSTEM_CONFIG` before it opens the cards. `t/CMakeLists.txt` registers `t_clearhbm` with `DISABLED TRUE`. CTest (the CMake test runner) and Slice then do not run it. `TRON_VERIFY_ECC` adds a check after the write.

cells.Values and default: Any value turns it on, also `0` and an empty value. The test does not parse the text. Unset: the test has no verify phase.
cells.Effect: After the write phase, the test runs one matrix multiply on each FPGA card. It fails when a result differs from the value that it computes from `TRON_POISON_BITS`. A comment in the test says that the verify phase is meaningful only after a write with a `TRON_POISON_BITS` value other than `0`. `t/CMakeLists.txt` registers `t_clearhbm` with `DISABLED TRUE`. CTest (the CMake test runner) and Slice then do not run it.

cells.Values and default: Path of the `rinzler_proxy` program. `t/proxy/run_suite.sh` resolves a relative path against the checkout root. `t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py` uses the text as it is. Unset: `gen/rinzler_proxy` in the checkout. Empty: `t/proxy/run_suite.sh` uses the same default, except in the mode `test_rzproxy.py lib`. `t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py` uses the empty text as the path.
cells.Effect: Selects the `rinzler_proxy` program that the test suites under `t/proxy` start. `t/proxy/run_suite.sh` exits with status 1 when the file is not executable, except in the mode `test_rzproxy.py lib`. CTest (the CMake test runner) sets it for `t_proxy_lib`, `t_proxy_llama31` and `t_proxy_gptoss` to the `rinzler_proxy` of the same build tree. In the mode `test_rzproxy.py lib`, the test of the real program skips when the file is missing.

cells.Values and default: Any text. The test searches for it inside the message content of the response. Unset: the test case skips this one check. Its other checks still run.
cells.Effect: The test case `rinzler_proxy decodes golden tokens over HTTP` checks that the message content of the HTTP response contains this text. An empty value always passes the check. The test case skips before it reads this variable when no model or no token ids are available. `TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH` and `TRON_GOLDEN_IDS` give them. The fallback model of `TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH` gives them too.

cells.Values and default: Integer token ids separated by commas, for example `9707,1879,128009`. Each item is parsed with `std::stoi`. An item without a leading number throws an exception. Unset: the list of token ids is empty when `TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH` is set. Then 5 test cases skip.
cells.Effect: Gives the token ids for the golden file (the JSON file of token ids that `rinzler_proxy` replays). 4 test cases use the whole list as the model output. 1 test case uses the last id as the output and the other ids as the prompt. The test reads it only when `TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH` is set. One test case needs at least 2 ids. A comment in the test says that the list must end with the end-of-sequence id of the served model. The test names the file in `TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS`.

Replaces the weights directory that `run_suite.sh` checks before it starts pytest. The script exits with status 1 when the directory is missing, except in the call `run_suite.sh test_rzproxy.py lib`. A value that differs from the default makes the script print a warning in every call. It changes this check only. The Python test code (`t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py`) does not read it and keeps the fixed root `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`. In the repository only `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py` sets it.

cells.Values and default: A model name, for example `shuyuej/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GPTQ`. It is not a file path. `rinzler_proxy` puts `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/` before the name. Unset: the test uses `shuyuej/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GPTQ` when that model is installed. Otherwise 9 test cases skip. Empty: the test starts `rinzler_proxy` without `--model-path`.
cells.Effect: Selects the model that the 9 HTTP test cases of `t_rinzler_proxy` serve. The test starts `rinzler_proxy` with `--model-path <name>:default:<name>`. Each request names this model. When it is set, the token ids come from `TRON_GOLDEN_IDS` only. The fallback model counts as installed when `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/shuyuej/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GPTQ` exists. The fallback uses the token ids `9707,1879,128009`.

rows.name: PERFETTO_CAPTURE_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION
rows.table: 4.4 Tests of Dice, Slice and CI scripts

cells.Values and default: Exactly `1` turns the requirement on. Any other text leaves it off. Unset: when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` is empty, or `traced` or `perfetto` in it is not executable, the script prints `SKIP integration` and exits with status 0.
cells.Effect: With `1`, the script prints `FAIL: integration required` and exits with status 1 when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` does not hold the executable Perfetto programs `traced` and `perfetto`. It does not skip the integration checks. CI sets `1` for the step `CI helper script tests` in `cmake-single-platform.yml` and `gcp-nix.yml`. The variable changes nothing when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` holds both programs.

rows.name: TRON_EXPECTED_NIXFMT_PATH
rows.table: 4.4 Tests of Dice, Slice and CI scripts

cells.Values and default: Nix store path (a path below `/nix/store`) of the `nixfmt` package. The test compares it as exact text with each whole line of a file. Unset: the test fails with `Expected upstream nixfmt path is missing` when `TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT` is `1`. Otherwise the test does not read it.
cells.Effect: The test searches the file that `TRON_LINT_CLOSURE_PATHS` names for a line equal to this path. When no line matches, the test fails with `Lint shell does not use nixfmt from the upstream package set`. `flake.nix` sets it to the `nixfmt` package in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).
